rows.text: No. 17/2003 Monetary Policy Committee's Mr. Bandid Nijathaworn, Assistant Thailand announced that the Monetary Policy economic developments and trends in order going forward.

The main issues discussed were 1. The MPC reviewed the latest data that economic growth in the first 4 months expanded significantly, income from major prices and volume, export grew robustly, improve.
However, tourism and hotel activity Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS).
In moderating, private investment growth remained more slowly than expected.
2. External stability remained strong further declines in foreign debt.
The current sharp reductions in tourism revenue lowered transfers balances also declined.
The baht appreciated line with other regional currencies.
3. The economic recovery thus far prices with headline inflation edging up to 1.9 April.
Core inflation remained subdued at 0.1 month.
The MPC expected core inflation to next 8 quarters and recognized the risk that core inflation may fall below target in the future.

4. The MPC assessed that the main risks to the Thai economy in the near term emanated from external uncertainties, in particular with respect to the fragility of economic recovery in main industrialized countries, the negative impact from Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) on regional economies and Thailand's tourism industry, and the possibility of further declines in the US dollar.

The MPC stressed the need to closely monitor these developments and take stock of their impact on the economy, while maintaining an accommodative stance of monetary policy supportive of economic growth going forward.
The MPC decided to maintain the 14-day repurchase rate at 1.75 per cent per annum.
